Use it when setting up or auditing a repository's engineering process - writing AGENTS.md, a pull-request template, CODEOWNERS, secret scanning (gitleaks), docs-check, dependency-bot (Renovate) config, PR-size limits, policy gates, phase gates - or when running build, test, lint and audit gates for Node, Next.js, React, React Native, Vue, Angular, .NET, Laravel/PHP, Flutter, Python/Django, Java/Spring, Go, Rust, Ruby/Rails, C/C++, Swift, Terraform or Docker projects, including monorepos. Also use it when the user wants these checks to run locally without paid CI and be proven in the pull request. A location/marketplace domain add-on is optional and loaded only on request.

# Engineering rules skill

A small universal core: rules, pull-request gates and a delivery loop that fit any software
project, in any language or framework. Detail is in `references/`; ready-to-copy files are in
`templates/` and `scripts/`. Load only what the task needs.

## When to use

- Start or audit a repository's engineering process (new or existing).
- Write or review `AGENTS.md`, the pull-request template, `CODEOWNERS`, CI gates.
- Add secret scanning, docs-check, PR-size limits, a dependency-bot config.
- Run stack gates (install, tests, build, lint, audit) on any repository, monorepos included.
- Plan work in phases and tasks, or run a phase gate.
- Prove the gates without hosted or paid CI.

Do not use it to invent product requirements, and do not load the domain file unless the
product needs it.

## The core in six lines

1. Work in small phases of numbered tasks; one task is about one pull request, about 400 lines or fewer.
2. Every task passes the gates before review: secret scan, docs-check, dependency-bot config, policy gates, flag expiry, PR size, plus stack gates.
3. Proof is a green CI run **or** the output of `local-proof.sh` pasted into the pull request (`--json` for machine-readable results). A gate that did not run is not proof.
4. Docs move with code (docs map, changelog); decisions are ADRs; a missing decision is an open question, never a guess.
5. Humans merge. Assistants never merge, on any CI level.
6. Anything not yet enforced is labelled **Planned**. Never present it as enforced.

The complete, binding rule set is `templates/AGENTS.md` (about 1.4k tokens). Read it in full before you
advise, review or change anything, and never reconstruct the rules from memory.

## What an agent does

| Request | Do this |
|---|---|
| "Set up the process in this repo" | Run `scripts/install.sh --target <repo>`; fill the placeholders; run `doctor.sh`, then `local-proof.sh`. |
| "Run the checks for this project" | Run `stack-gates.sh`: it detects the stack (Node, Next.js, React, .NET, Laravel, Flutter, Python, Java, Go, Rust, Ruby, C/C++, Swift, Terraform, Docker) and runs its gates. |
| "Add a rule" | Check `references/rules-index.md` first. Add it to `AGENTS.md`, add a row to `docs/rules-compliance.md` with an honest status, and write an ADR. |
| "Review this pull request" | Check the Definition of Done in the template, the gate rows, and that exception labels have a written reason. |
| "CI is down or out of minutes" | Follow `references/continuity.md`; run `local-proof.sh`; do not relax a gate. |
| "A gate failed" | Read `references/fixing-failures.md`; run `local-proof.sh --json`, fix each `FAIL` at its cause, never weaken the gate. |
| "Update the installed rules" | Run `scripts/install.sh --target <repo> --update`: scripts and workflows are refreshed, your edits are kept (new versions land as `.new`). |
| "End of phase" | Run `references/phase-gate.md` and log the result. |

## Hard rules for the agent

- Never merge, never allowlist a secret, never edit a synced rules file in place.
- Never skip or weaken a gate to finish faster; propose an ADR instead.
- Never add real names, hosts, tokens, account ids or private task ids to files. Use
  placeholders: `<org>`, `<owner>`, `<project>`, `@<owner>`, `api.example.com`.
- Keep Planned items marked Planned. Keep the default path free of domain rules.

## Where things are

| Need | File |
|---|---|
| The delivery loop, roles, branch protection | `references/workflow.md` |
| Every rule, scope, check and status | `references/rules-index.md` |
| Run the gates locally and paste proof | `references/local-proof.md` |
| What to do when a gate fails | `references/fixing-failures.md` |
| Phase gate checklist | `references/phase-gate.md` |
| CI fallback levels, dependency register, CI-minute rules | `references/continuity.md` |
| Stack gates for Node, React, Vue, Angular, Next.js, React Native, .NET, Laravel/PHP, Flutter, Python, Java, Go, Rust, Ruby, C/C++, Swift, Terraform, Docker | `references/stacks/README.md` and `references/stacks/<stack>.md` |
| Location, multi-country, marketplace rules (optional) | `references/domain-optional.md` |
| Starter `AGENTS.md`, PR template, CODEOWNERS, hooks, scanner and bot config, CI workflows, docs starters, assistant bridge files | `templates/` |
| Gate scripts, installer, doctor, self-test | `scripts/` |

## Adoption in one paragraph

From the target repository run `bash <skill>/scripts/install.sh --target . --profile standard`;
fill the placeholders (owners, thresholds, docs map, CI provider, tool pins); run
`bash .github/scripts/doctor.sh`, then `bash .github/scripts/local-proof.sh`; open the first
pull request with the proof pasted in.

---
## FILE: skills/engineering-rules/templates/AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md: engineering rules

This file is the single rules file for the repository. People and coding
assistants (any tool) follow it the same way. Words: **MUST** is binding,
**SHOULD** needs a written reason to skip, **MAY** is optional.

> Starter from `engineering-rules-skill`. Fill in the `<placeholders>` and delete
> what you do not use. Detail lives in the skill's `references/` folder (installed with the
> skill, not in this repository); this file stays short on purpose. Items marked **Planned** are not enforced yet.

## 1. Scope and ownership

- This file is the only rules file. Do not create a second, competing one.
- In a multi-repository project one repository (`infra`) owns the canonical copy;
  the others carry a byte-identical copy and MUST NOT edit it in place.
- Rules about location, multi-country or on-demand marketplaces are **not** part of
  this file. Add them only if your product needs them (`references/domain-optional.md`).

## 2. Delivery

1. Work in small phases made of numbered tasks. One task is about one pull
   request and under about 400 changed lines.
2. Every task passes the gates in section 5 before review.
3. After each phase, run the phase gate (`references/phase-gate.md`). A failure
   blocks the next phase.
4. Assistants MUST NOT merge. A human reviews and merges.
5. If a rule is unclear or a decision is missing, write an open question. Do not
   guess and do not invent a requirement.

## 3. Definition of done

A change is done when:

- [ ] behavior is covered by tests that fail without the change;
- [ ] the gates in section 5 pass (CI, or the local proof in section 6);
- [ ] docs changed with the code and `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry (or the title type is `chore`/`ci`/`test`);
- [ ] no secret, token, private host or personal data was added;
- [ ] a new dependency, a deviation from this file, or a new pattern has a decision record (ADR);
- [ ] the pull request is within the size limit, or carries the reason label and a written reason.

## 4. Core rules

- **Secrets.** MUST NOT be committed. A finding is rotated, never allowlisted.
- **Dependencies.** Versions are pinned and lockfiles committed. Prerelease
  versions need an ADR. Updates come through the dependency bot and are reviewed.
- **Configuration is data.** Product code MUST NOT hard-code a currency, region,
  time zone, dial prefix, host or named place. Read them from configuration.
- **Failure handling.** Every network call has a timeout. Retry only idempotent
  operations. Logs MUST NOT contain secrets or personal data.
- **Feature flags.** Each flag has an owner, a purpose and an expiry date. An
  expired flag fails the check until it is removed or extended with a reason.
- **Documentation travels with code.** The docs map (`docs/docs-map.yml`) says which docs
  a code path needs.
- **Decisions.** Record them as ADRs. An unresolved decision is an open question.
- **CI and tools.** GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs and downloaded tools to checksum-verified
  versions. CI runs once per change, every job has a timeout, and a superseded run is cancelled.
- **Runbooks.** Every alert has a runbook. A runbook marked Planned is a promise, not a procedure.
- **Duplication.** Copy-paste above the threshold is extracted (stack adapters set the tool and number).

## 5. Gates

| Gate | What it checks | Run locally | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Secret scan | full git history, redacted output, no ignore file | `.github/scripts/gitleaks-scan.sh` | Enforced |
| docs-check | required docs, docs map, changelog, markdown lint, internal links | `.github/scripts/docs-check.sh` | Enforced |
| Dependency-bot config | `renovate.json` valid and extends the shared preset | `.github/scripts/renovate-config-check.sh` | Enforced |
| Policy gates | prerelease dependencies, environment literals | `.github/scripts/policy-gates.mjs` | Enforced |
| Flag expiry | every flag has owner, purpose, future expiry | `.github/scripts/feature-flag-expiry.mjs` | Enforced |
| PR size | counted lines under the limit (lockfiles, snapshots excluded) | `.github/scripts/pr-size-check.sh` | Enforced |
| Stack gates | install, tests, build; lint, types, format, audit in strict | `.github/scripts/stack-gates.sh` | Enforced |
| Phase gate | whole-file compliance walk and smoke test | `references/phase-gate.md` | Manual |

Anything not in this table is **Planned**, not enforced.

## 6. Proof without paid CI

Hosted CI is optional. The same scripts run on a developer machine. When CI cannot
run, run `.github/scripts/local-proof.sh`, paste its output into the pull request, and the
reviewer treats it as the proof. A gate that did not run is not proof.
Fallback levels: `references/continuity.md`.

## 7. Governance

- Changing this file needs a pull request, an ADR for the reason, and an update
  to `docs/rules-compliance.md` (which rule is enforced by which check).
- Exceptions use the labels `no-docs-needed` and `pr-size-reason`, each with a
  written reason in the pull request. The reviewer accepts or rejects the reason.
- Owners of sensitive paths are listed in `CODEOWNERS`.

## 8. Optional adapters

Stack gates run with `.github/scripts/stack-gates.sh` (details in `references/stacks/`).
Domain: `references/domain-optional.md`. Load them only when your project uses them.

---
## FILE: skills/engineering-rules/references/rules-index.md

# Rules index

Every rule, its scope, how it is checked, and its honest status. This is the map to
copy into your `docs/rules-compliance.md`. The **Scope** column decides where a rule
lives:

- **Universal**: any software project. These are the default path.
- **Stack**: only if you use that stack. Detail is in [`stacks/`](stacks/README.md).
- **Domain**: only for location-based, multi-country or on-demand marketplace
  products. Detail is in [`domain-optional.md`](domain-optional.md). Never part of the default path.

**Status.** *Enforced*: a script fails the pull request. *Implemented*: the tool
exists but is not wired as a required check until you do it. *Review*: a reviewer
checks it. *Ops*: a runbook or a schedule. *Planned*: not enforced yet; never present
it as a rule that holds.

## Universal

| # | Rule | Scope | Checked by | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U1 | One rules file; copies elsewhere are byte-identical and never edited in place | Universal | `scripts/sync-rules-file.sh` (multi-repo), review | Implemented |
| U2 | Small phases and tasks; one pull request is about 400 lines or fewer | Universal | `pr-size-check.sh` (warn 400, fail 800 with reason label) | Enforced |
| U3 | Task gates pass before review; proof is CI or a pasted local proof | Universal | `project-gates.yml`, `local-proof.sh` | Enforced |
| U4 | Phase gate after every phase; a failure blocks the next phase | Universal | [`phase-gate.md`](phase-gate.md), compliance log | Review |
| U5 | Assistants never merge; humans review and merge | Universal | branch protection, CODEOWNERS | Review |
| U6 | No secrets in git; full-history scan; no ignore file; rotate, never allowlist | Universal | `gitleaks-scan.sh`, `gitleaks.toml`, pre-commit hook | Enforced |
| U7 | Docs travel with code: required docs, docs map, changelog, markdown lint, internal links | Universal | `docs-check.sh` | Enforced |
| U8 | Dependencies pinned, lockfiles committed, updates through the bot | Universal | `renovate-config-check.sh`; frozen install in stack gates | Enforced |
| U9 | No prerelease dependency without an ADR and an allowlist entry | Universal | `policy-gates.mjs` | Enforced |
| U10 | Configuration is data: no hard-coded currency, region, time zone, dial prefix or named place in product code | Universal | `policy-gates.mjs` + `policy/country-literals.json` | Enforced |
| U11 | Feature flags have owner, purpose and expiry; expired flags fail | Universal | `feature-flag-expiry.mjs` | Enforced |
| U12 | A flag still read in code after it is retired fails | Universal | needs a code scan per stack | Planned |
| U13 | Decisions are ADRs; an unresolved decision is an open question, not a guess | Universal | review | Review |
| U14 | Exceptions only by label plus written reason (`no-docs-needed`, `pr-size-reason`) | Universal | docs-check, PR size, review | Enforced |
| U15 | Failure handling: timeouts on network calls, retries only for idempotent operations, no secrets or personal data in logs | Universal | review; stack lint rules where available | Review |
| U16 | Actions pinned to commit SHAs; downloaded tools pinned and checksum-verified | Universal | dependency bot digest pinning, `install-release-tool.sh` | Enforced |
| U17 | Cross-language artifacts that must stay byte-identical have a SHA-256 lock | Universal | `assert-sha256-lock.mjs` in a project check | Implemented |
| U18 | CI-minute hygiene: one run per change, cancel superseded runs, skip heavy steps on docs-only changes, timeouts, caches | Universal | `project-gates.yml` pattern | Review |
| U19 | Delivery continuity: every outside dependency has detect, fallback, switch-back and a runbook | Universal | [`continuity.md`](continuity.md), `continuity-check.sh` | Ops |
| U20 | Runbooks per alert; `Planned` status is honest until verified | Universal | review | Review |
| U21 | Rules file changes need an ADR and an update of the compliance table | Universal | docs-map rule on `AGENTS.md` | Enforced |

## Stack gates (all stacks)

Run by `scripts/stack-gates.sh`, one engine per stack. See [`stacks/README.md`](stacks/README.md).

| # | Rule | Scope | Checked by | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | A clean, locked install works; lockfiles are committed | Stack | `deps` gate (all engines) | Enforced |
| S2 | Tests pass | Stack | `test` gate | Enforced |
| S3 | The production build succeeds | Stack | `build` gate | Enforced |
| S4 | A gate that did not run is never a pass: required gates fail on SKIP and NOT RUN | Stack | `STACK_REQUIRE` policy in `stack-gates.sh` | Enforced |
| S5 | Formatting, lint and type checks pass | Stack | `format`, `lint`, `types` gates | Enforced in profile `strict`; otherwise listed in `STACK_REQUIRE` |
| S6 | No known-vulnerable runtime dependency | Stack | `audit` gate (npm, pnpm, yarn, composer, dotnet; cargo-audit, pip-audit, govulncheck, bundler-audit and OWASP when installed) | Enforced in `strict`; NOT RUN when the tool is missing |
| S7 | Client bundle contains no private backend host | Stack (Next.js, web) | `bundle-scan` gate | Enforced when `API_BASE_URL` is set |
| S8 | No keystore, credentials file or private key tracked; no literal signing password; no cleartext URL | Stack (React Native, Flutter) | `secrets-files` gate | Enforced |
| S9 | Python requirements are pinned; Django model changes have migrations | Stack (Python) | `pinned`, `migrations` gates | Enforced |
| S10 | `go.mod` is tidy; `Cargo.lock` is committed for binaries | Stack (Go, Rust) | `mod-tidy`, `deps` gates | Enforced |
| S11 | Layer dependencies and banned APIs (architecture tests) | Stack | tests you write in your language | Planned |
| S12 | Migration SQL linted and applied to an empty database in CI | Stack | depends on your database | Planned |
| S13 | Container images build from a clean context | Stack | `docker build` job you add | Planned |
| S14 | Time-dependent tests run under several time zones | Stack | a CI matrix you add (`TZ=`) | Planned |
| S15 | Installable test builds with a checksum, built on demand (mobile) | Stack | a `workflow_dispatch` job you add | Planned |

## Domain (optional)

Rules for location, multi-country and on-demand marketplace products are listed in
[`domain-optional.md`](domain-optional.md) with their own status. They are **not**
counted in the Universal rows above, and no gate in the default path depends on them.

---
## FILE: skills/engineering-rules/references/stacks/README.md

# Stack gates

One command runs the right checks for whatever your repository contains:

```bash
bash .github/scripts/stack-gates.sh          # every stack it finds
bash .github/scripts/stack-gates.sh --list   # just show what it detects
```

It detects the stacks, runs the standard gates for each, and prints one row per gate.
Monorepos are handled: a `web/` (Next.js), an `api/` (Go) and a `mobile/` (Expo) folder in
one repository each get their own run.

## The gates

| Gate | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `deps` | Does a clean, locked install work? (lockfile committed, frozen install) |
| `format` | Is the code formatted? |
| `lint` | Does the linter or analyzer pass? |
| `types` | Does the type checker or static analyzer pass? |
| `test` | Do the tests pass? |
| `build` | Does the production build succeed? |
| `audit` | Are there known vulnerabilities in the dependencies? |
| extras | Stack-specific: `bundle-scan`, `secrets-files`, `migrations`, `mod-tidy`, `syntax`, `pinned`... |

## Results

| Result | Meaning |
|---|---|
| PASS | ran and succeeded |
| FAIL | ran and failed (the last lines of the log are printed) |
| SKIP | nothing to run (no script, no config) |
| NOT RUN | applies, but a tool or network service is unavailable or rate-limited |
| N/A | does not apply to this stack (PHP has no build step) |
| WARN | advice only |

**Required gates.** `STACK_REQUIRE` (default `deps,test,build`) lists the gates that must
PASS. For those, SKIP and NOT RUN count as a failure: "nothing ran" never looks green. A
project with no tests fails `test` until it has some. Profiles change the list:
`lite` requires `deps,test`; `strict` adds `format,lint,types,audit`.

For network-dependent gates, recognized HTTP 429 and rate-limit responses are recorded as
NOT RUN rather than as a command failure. NOT RUN still fails when that gate is required.

## Configure

Put values in `.github/engineering-rules.env` (the installer writes it from a profile):

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `STACK_REQUIRE` | gates that must pass |
| `STACK_STRICT=1` | also require format, lint, types, audit |
| `STACK_CMD_<GATE>` | replace a gate's command: `STACK_CMD_TEST="make test"` |
| `STACK_SKIP_GATES` | switch gates off on purpose (they leave the required list) |
| `STACK_EXCLUDE` | path prefixes to ignore, for example `examples/ docs/site` |
| `STACK_FAST=1` | skip `build`, `audit`, `e2e` (a quick loop while coding) |
| `AUDIT_LEVEL` | minimum severity that fails an audit |

An explicit project list in `.github/engineering-rules.stacks` (`node:web`, `go:api`) replaces detection.

## Supported stacks and how well each one is tested

| Stack | Frameworks | Reference | Tested with |
|---|---|---|---|
| node | Node.js, React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, NestJS, Express, Vite | [node.md](node.md) | real npm, real React/Vite project |
| nextjs | Next.js | [nextjs.md](nextjs.md) | real Next.js build; the audit gate caught real advisories |
| react-native | React Native, Expo | [react-native.md](react-native.md) | real node engine and secret-file check; Expo CLI stubbed |
| dotnet | ASP.NET Core, console, libraries | [dotnet.md](dotnet.md) | real .NET SDK (restore from a local source) |
| php | Laravel, Symfony, Composer packages | [laravel.md](laravel.md) | real PHP and Composer; Pint, PHPStan and `artisan` stubbed |
| flutter | Flutter, Dart | [flutter.md](flutter.md) | command-level tests with stubbed SDK; real run happens in the repository CI matrix |
| python | Django, FastAPI, Flask, libraries | [python.md](python.md) | real pip, pytest, ruff |
| java | Spring Boot, Maven, Gradle, Kotlin | [java.md](java.md) | command-level tests with stubbed build tools |
| go | Go modules | [go.md](go.md) | real Go toolchain |
| rust | Cargo | [rust.md](rust.md) | real cargo, rustfmt, clippy |
| ruby | Rails, gems | [ruby.md](ruby.md) | real Ruby and Bundler; Rails and RuboCop stubbed |
| cpp | C and C++ (CMake) | [cpp.md](cpp.md) | real cmake, g++, cppcheck, clang-format |
| terraform | Terraform, OpenTofu | [terraform.md](terraform.md) | real OpenTofu |
| docker | Dockerfiles | [docker.md](docker.md) | real hadolint |
| swift | Swift Package Manager | [swift.md](swift.md) | command-level tests with a stubbed toolchain |

"Stubbed" means the engine's commands, order and failure handling are verified, but the real
tool was not run in the test environment. See `docs/testing.md` in the repository for the
exact matrix and how to run it yourself.

## Add a stack

See `CONTRIBUTING.md`: an engine is one file in `scripts/stacks/<name>.sh`, one workflow in
`templates/stacks/<name>/ci.yml`, one reference here, and a good and a bad fixture in `tests/`.

---
## FILE: skills/engineering-rules/references/fixing-failures.md

# Fixing failures

What to do when a gate fails. Read the message first: every gate prints the file, the rule
or the command that failed. Never "fix" a failure by weakening the gate.

## Core gates

| Gate and message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Secret scan: `project-dotenv-file`, `project-signing-key-file`, a default gitleaks rule | A secret or a secret-like file is in git history | **Rotate the secret first.** If the branch is not shared, rewrite it so the commit disappears (`git reset --soft`, recommit without the file). Add the file to `.gitignore` and commit a `.env.example` with names only. Never add `.gitleaksignore`. |
| Secret scan: `Shallow clone` | CI fetched only the last commit | `fetch-depth: 0` (GitHub), `GIT_DEPTH: 0` (GitLab) |
| Secret scan fails on old history in an existing repository | Old secrets were committed long ago | Rotate them, record an ADR, then set `SECRET_SCAN_FROM=<adoption commit>` in `.github/engineering-rules.env`. The scan then covers newer commits only, and says so loudly. |
| docs-check: `code changed under "<glob>" without a change in: ...` | Code changed, its docs did not | Update one of the listed docs in the same pull request. If no doc is affected, add the label `no-docs-needed` with a written reason. |
| docs-check: `CHANGELOG.md has no entry` | A `feat` or `fix` pull request without a changelog line | Add a line under `Unreleased`. Titles of type `chore`, `ci`, `test` are exempt. |
| docs-check: markdown lint | A changed markdown file breaks a rule | Fix the file (the message names rule and line). Old files are not linted in profiles `lite` and `standard`. |
| docs-check: required doc missing | A file from `required-docs.json` is absent | Create it, or remove it from the list with an ADR. |
| Policy gates: `currency code literal`, `region code`, `time-zone id`, `dial prefix`, `named place` | Business configuration is typed into code | Move the value to configuration (environment, settings table). If it is a false positive (a test, a seed), add the path pattern to `.github/policy/country-literals.json`. |
| Policy gates: `... is a prerelease` | A beta, rc or preview dependency | Use a stable version, or write an ADR and add the package to `.github/policy/prerelease-allow.json`. |
| Flag expiry | A feature flag is past its `expiresOn` date | Remove the flag and its code, or extend the date and write why. |
| PR size: `changes N lines, above 800` | The pull request is too large | Split it. Move generated or pasted data out of the change. If it cannot be split, add `pr-size-reason` and explain in the description. |
| Renovate config | `renovate.json` is invalid or does not extend the preset | Run `bash .github/scripts/renovate-config-check.sh`; the validator names the key. |

## Stack gates (all stacks)

| Result | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `deps` FAIL: no lockfile | An application without a lockfile | Commit it (`package-lock.json`, `Cargo.lock`, `composer.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`, `pubspec.lock`, `uv.lock`...). |
| `deps` FAIL: install failed | The locked install does not work | Run the same command locally (the output shows it). Usually the lockfile is out of sync with the manifest: regenerate and commit it. |
| `test` SKIP: no tests | Required gate has nothing to run | Add tests, or set `STACK_REQUIRE` to drop `test` with an ADR. A project with no tests should say so. |
| `NOT RUN` | A tool or the network is missing | Install the tool (the message names it). In CI add the setup step; locally use the package manager. |
| `format` FAIL | Code is not formatted | Run the formatter (`prettier --write`, `gofmt -w`, `dotnet format`, `cargo fmt`, `dart format .`, `ruff format`, `pint`, `tofu fmt`). |
| `lint` FAIL | The linter or analyzer found issues | Fix them. A rule you disagree with is changed in the tool's own config, in a reviewed pull request. |
| `audit` FAIL | A known-vulnerable dependency | Update it. If no fix exists, record an ADR with the mitigation and add the advisory exception in the tool's own file. |
| `bundle-scan` FAIL (Next.js) | The private backend host is in the client bundle | Move the call behind a server route; keep the host in a server-only variable. |
| `secrets-files` FAIL (mobile) | A keystore, credentials file or `http://` URL is tracked | Remove it, rotate the key, use a secret store. |
| `migrations` FAIL (Django) | A model changed without a migration | `python manage.py makemigrations` and commit. |
| `mod-tidy` FAIL (Go) | `go.mod` or `go.sum` is not tidy | `go mod tidy` and commit. |
| `pinned` FAIL (Python) | A requirement without `==` | Pin it (`pip freeze` or a lock tool). |

## For an AI agent

1. Run `bash .github/scripts/local-proof.sh --json` and read `gates[].status`.
2. For each `FAIL`, run that gate alone (`references/local-proof.md` lists the commands) and read its output.
3. Fix the cause. Do not edit a gate, a profile, an exception label or the pins to make it pass.
4. If a fix needs a decision (a new dependency, a rule deviation, a larger pull request), write an open question or an ADR and stop.
5. Re-run until every row is `PASS` (or `NA`). Paste the Markdown proof into the pull request.
